name: Base Rates

brand.tagline: Before you decide, see what usually happens: graded base rates for life, work and policy choices, and your own forecasting record. Run on Ultrastable, the foundation for any autonomous system.

idea: An encyclopedia of reference classes (new businesses surviving five years, megaprojects on budget, diets kept after a year, reforms delivering their stated aim), each with its base rate, source and grade. An hourly beat re-reads each entry's source series for new releases and surfaces newer studies; readers' guesses before the reveal measure which base rates surprise most and order the site.
goals: encyclopedia of 50 graded base rates with guess-first entries
decision companion: name a plan, get its reference class and a pre-mortem
positioning: People and institutions predict from the story in front of them and ignore how often such things usually go; showing the reference class first makes forecasts better. Same shape as Unlearn and Practical Solutions: guess first, graded evidence, a loop that keeps checking, no accounts or trackers.

system_test.loop: An hourly beat re-reads each entry's source series for new releases and surfaces newer studies; readers' guesses before the reveal measure which base rates surprise most and order the site.
system_test.measure: share of entries whose source series was re-read within 7 days, target 1.0; share of readers whose guess missed the base rate by more than half, published per entry
system_test.upkeep: new studies, data releases and evaluations arrive every week, sources rot and entries must be re-graded
system_test.run_cost: 5 USD a month for the back end

decision companion: name a plan, get its reference class and a pre-mortem
depth.hook: Guess first: how often do new restaurants survive five years? Then the base rate, and how far off you were. Every person misses some, and the miss is the hook.
depth.public_good: People and governments make better decisions about money, health and policy when they see how such things usually go; it counters overconfident plans that waste public money.
